findings.description: The github.actor == pull_request.user.login check applies to all pull_request sub-events (opened, ready_for_review, synchronize), but the adjacent comment justifies it only for synchronize ("a push by anyone else to that branch fires synchronize"). For ready_for_review specifically, a trusted maintainer other than the PR author marking another trusted author's draft ready has github.actor != pull_request.user.login, so the pull_request-triggered path is skipped (the @claude review comment path still works). This fails closed, not open, so it's not a security gap, but the implementation is broader than the stated rationale covers.

Same actor-equality broadening as in the emitted template applies to this repo's dogfood OWNER_GATE (github.actor == github.repository_owner on the pull_request leg), for the same reason: it's applied to all pull_request sub-events though the rationale only covers synchronize.

fromJSON('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]') is repeated verbatim in both branches of the same if: expression. Not actionable today since GitHub Actions' env context isn't available in job-level if: conditions, and the two sites are 4 lines apart so edit drift is unlikely, but flagging for visibility if the trust list ever needs to change.

process_issues.description: This run's config-restore step replaced templates/ with the merge-base's copy (per RESTORE_PATHS in .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml) but did not save a pre-restore snapshot to .claude-pr/templates/, unlike CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json which were preserved there. Reviewers had to be briefed to use git diff/gh pr diff instead of Read for templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml. Did not block the review since the diff commands are authoritative regardless, but worth checking whether the 'Restore startup config from base' step's cp -R is actually running for every RESTORE_PATHS entry.
